description: What the catalog budget suite must notice: an alias of a gateway is relied on, an input limit or an output reserve is forgotten, the output cap is raised or a useless one is used, the owner's window loses to the catalog's, the source of a window is mislabelled, the facts do not reach the snapshot, a profile fork or the adapter or the context meter or the tool selection reads only the owner's window, a preset hard-codes a window again, the agent ignores the facts or takes an output cap on trust, the price estimate is dropped or is not fixed for the run.

mutations.name: B1
mutations.what: a gateway's alias of a maker's model is relied on like an exact id

mutations.name: B2
mutations.what: an input limit below the window is ignored (the whole window is planned on)

patches.old: const limited = window !== null && Number.isInteger(info.maxInput) && info.maxInput > 0 && info.maxInput < window;

mutations.name: B3
mutations.what: the output the agent reserves is left out of the capacity under an input limit

mutations.name: B4
mutations.what: the model's output cap raises what the agent asks for above its own ceiling

mutations.name: B5
mutations.what: an output cap too small to write in is used as a limit

mutations.name: B6
mutations.what: the catalog's window wins over the one the owner typed

mutations.name: B7
mutations.what: a window the owner typed is said to come from the catalog

mutations.name: B8
mutations.what: the snapshot of the provider carries no prices

mutations.name: B9
mutations.what: a task profile's fork does not use the catalog of its parent

mutations.name: B10
mutations.what: the adapter trims to the owner's window only

patches.old: const contextWindowTokens = this.effectiveContextWindow(); // what the adapter trims
patches.new: const contextWindowTokens = this.contextWindowTokens; // what the adapter trims

mutations.name: B11
mutations.what: the context meter reads the owner's window only

patches.old:
const window = this.effectiveContextWindow();
    return { estimated: true,
patches.new:
const window = this.contextWindowTokens;
    return { estimated: true,

mutations.name: B12
mutations.what: the Anthropic preset hard-codes a window of 200,000 again

mutations.name: B13
mutations.what: the tool selection reads the owner's window only

mutations.name: B14
mutations.what: the agent plans without the capacity the provider gives

mutations.name: B15
mutations.what: the agent ignores the output cap the provider gives

patches.old: outputLimit: Number.isSafeInteger(cap) && cap >= 1024 ? Math.min(cap, MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS) : MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS,

mutations.name: B16
mutations.what: the price of a run is read again for every response instead of fixed at its start

mutations.name: B17
mutations.what: the catalog's prices never reach the cost of a task

mutations.name: B18
mutations.what: an output cap above the agent's ceiling, or a useless one, is taken from the provider on trust

patches.old: outputLimit: Number.isSafeInteger(cap) && cap >= 1024 ? Math.min(cap, MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS) : MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS,

mutations.name: B19
mutations.what: the capacity of a model with a small input limit adds the whole output to the limit, and plans a prompt the model refuses

patches.old: const modelCapacity = limited && ceiling !== null ? capacityWithinInput(info.maxInput, outputLimit, ceiling) : ceiling;

mutations.name: B20
mutations.what: the margin the budget keeps is forgotten when the capacity is fitted to the input limit

patches.old: const promptFor = (capacity) => capacity - plannedOutputFor(capacity, outputLimit) - safetyMarginFor(capacity);

mutations.name: B21
mutations.what: the capacity fitted to the input limit is one that plans a prompt over the limit

patches.old: if (promptFor(middle) <= maxInput) fits = middle; else over = middle;
patches.new: if (promptFor(middle) <= maxInput + 64) fits = middle; else over = middle;

mutations.name: B22
mutations.what: the budget of a run keeps another margin than the capacity was fitted for (the two definitions drift apart)

mutations.name: B23
mutations.what: the floor is forgotten: a price that rises above 32,000 tokens stops the plan at 32,000, too little for the agent

patches.old: const stop = rise === null ? null : Math.max(PRICE_CAP_FLOOR_TOKENS, rise.aboveTokens);
patches.new: const stop = rise === null ? null : rise.aboveTokens;

mutations.name: B24
mutations.what: the highest price rise is taken instead of the first one (the plan crosses the first cliff)

mutations.name: B25
mutations.what: a tier that is cheaper than the base price is taken for a price rise

mutations.name: B26
mutations.what: a rise of the output price alone is not a price rise

mutations.name: B27
mutations.what: a rise of the input price alone is not a price rise

mutations.name: B28
mutations.what: the price rise is found but the plan is not stopped at it

mutations.name: B29
mutations.what: a stop that lowers nothing (the price rises where the window ends) is reported as one

patches.old: const stopped = stop !== null && stop < modelCapacity;
patches.new: const stopped = stop !== null && stop <= modelCapacity;

mutations.name: B30
mutations.what: the floor is lower than the Hub says (64,000)

mutations.name: B31
mutations.what: the answer does not say that the floor lifted the stop

mutations.name: B32
mutations.what: the stop is worked out from the window instead of from what the model allows (an input limit is forgotten)

patches.old: const stopped = stop !== null && stop < modelCapacity;
patches.new: const stopped = stop !== null && stop < (window ?? modelCapacity);

mutations.name: B33
mutations.what: the model-info route does not say what the model itself allows

mutations.name: B34
mutations.what: the model-info route does not say which price rise stopped the plan

mutations.name: B35
mutations.what: a price tier whose size is not a whole positive number is taken for a boundary
